Decision Inputs.A1: Decisions the Risk Team Must Make Before Viewing Results
Decision Inputs.B4: Minimum probability all 10 payments are full and on time
Decision Inputs.C4: Defines 'high degree of certainty' for the mandatory operating commitment
Decision Inputs.F4: Wharton requires a 'high degree of certainty'; team defines this as at least 95% joint success across all ten payments.
Decision Inputs.B5: Minimum probability a full operating reserve exists at start of 2033
Decision Inputs.C5: Separates pre-2033 accumulation risk from later payment risk
Decision Inputs.F5: Require at least 95% of simulated paths to have enough assets in 2033 to establish the full matched-payment operating reserve.
Decision Inputs.B6: Maximum mean unpaid dollars in chosen worst tail
Decision Inputs.C6: Controls severity, not just frequency, of failure
Decision Inputs.F6: Evaluate the worst 5% of simulated paths. Within that tail, the mean total unpaid operating-payment shortfall may not exceed $50,000.
Decision Inputs.C7: Prevents a candidate from passing only because payments survive despite intolerable portfolio losses
Decision Inputs.F7: Cap the 95th-percentile peak-to-trough investment loss at 30% so a candidate cannot pass solely by eventually recovering from severe losses.
Decision Inputs.B8: Maximum probability a payment requires sale of risky assets
Decision Inputs.C8: Protects liquidity and reduces forced selling during drawdowns
Decision Inputs.F8: With a matched-payment reserve, forced risky-asset sales should be exceptional. A 5% cap aligns with the 95% full-reserve success requirement.
Decision Inputs.B9: Maximum stock allocation across years / de-risking states
Decision Inputs.C9: Sets the ex-ante risk ceiling candidate designers cannot exceed
Decision Inputs.F9: Allow meaningful pre-2033 growth but prevent an equity-dominant strategy. Candidates must de-risk as the 2033 funding date approaches.
Decision Inputs.B10: Minimum retained share of post-reserve surplus
Decision Inputs.C10: Preserves financial flexibility instead of sending every remaining dollar to facility
Decision Inputs.F10: Keep at least 25% of post-reserve surplus for flexibility; a facility contribution should not consume nearly all remaining assets.
Decision Inputs.B11: Minimum payment success in each mandatory stress
Decision Inputs.C11: Requires the strategy to remain viable in adverse scenarios
Decision Inputs.F11: Require at least 90% payment success even under each predefined adverse stress. This is intentionally below the 95% base-case gate because stresses are conditional adverse scenarios.
Decision Inputs.C12: Defines how the 2033 reserve is constructed
Decision Inputs.B13: Allow reserve top-ups from unreserved assets?
Decision Inputs.C13: Defines whether retained/facility-side assets may support the reserve after losses
Decision Inputs.F13: Allow retained/unreserved assets to top up the reserve when needed because the operating commitment has priority over discretionary facility funding.
Decision Inputs.C14: Adds an absolute flexibility buffer if percentage-only retention is insufficient
Decision Inputs.F14: Retain at least $50,000 after the reserve when the percentage floor alone would leave too little flexibility; facility contribution is zero if the floor cannot be preserved.
Decision Inputs.B15: Issuer / single-stock and sector concentration limits
Decision Inputs.C15: Broad stock allocation alone cannot control idiosyncratic concentration risk
Decision Inputs.F15: Limit idiosyncratic concentration: no individual stock above 5% of total portfolio and no sector above 20% of total portfolio.

Risk Policy.B4: Minimum probability all ten $50k payments are full and on time
Risk Policy.F4: Wharton requires 'high degree of certainty'; exact percentage is a team proposal.
Risk Policy.B5: Minimum probability full reserve exists at start of 2033
Risk Policy.F5: Separates reserve formation risk from later payment performance.
Risk Policy.B6: Maximum mean unpaid dollars in the chosen worst tail
Risk Policy.F6: Worst-tail severity limit: use the worst 5% of simulated paths and cap mean total unpaid operating-payment shortfall at $50,000.
Risk Policy.B7: Limit on 95th percentile of maximum investment drawdown
Risk Policy.F7: 30% cap on 95th-percentile maximum investment drawdown; keeps severe path losses bounded independently of payment success.
Risk Policy.B8: Maximum probability payment needs risky-asset sale
Risk Policy.F8: 5% maximum probability that an operating payment requires a risky-asset sale; aligned with the 95% reserve-establishment gate.
Risk Policy.B9: Maximum stock allocation across years and de-risking states
Risk Policy.F9: 65% maximum total stock exposure; candidates then de-risk materially before 2033.
Risk Policy.B10: Classes supported by supplied packet/engine candidate design
Risk Policy.F10: Engine worksheets are structured around stocks, Treasuries and cash. WInS eligibility may be broader.
Risk Policy.B11: Minimum retained share of post-reserve surplus
Risk Policy.F11: Retain at least 25% of post-reserve surplus for flexibility; use a $50,000 retained-dollar floor as an additional candidate rule.
Risk Policy.B12: Minimum payment success in each mandatory stress
Risk Policy.F12: Require at least 90% payment success under every mandatory stress scenario.
Risk Policy.B16: 95% one-sided confidence bound for probability gates; target <=0.5 percentage-point confidence half-width. Use at least 50,000 simulation paths per candidate if computationally feasible.
Risk Policy.D16: Payment-success target is NOT the same thing as a confidence bound
Risk Policy.B17: Single-stock cap 5% of total portfolio; sector cap 20% of total portfolio.
Risk Policy.B18: Do not mark approved until preset rules are reviewed before candidate results.
